title: Pyruvate kinase and neural energy
summary: Mitapivat as a conditional ex vivo comparator in WWOX loss of function.

graph.evidence: Purified PKM2 responds. Rat brain exposure is low.
graph.inference: Blood response cannot identify neural isoform engagement.
graph.hypothesis: An activatable neural PKM2 pool could aid recovery.
graph.experiment: Measure local parent, PK flux and ATP at matched activity.

evidence: Half-maximal activation was 13 nM for WT erythrocyte PKR and 38 nM for PKM2 in one assay panel. PKM1 was unmeasured. Total rat brain/plasma AUC ratios were 0.057 and 0.091.
inference: A cross-species sensitivity requires 20% free brain parent at the modeled peak and 63% at the mean to reach 38 nM. These are conditional values. H3 activity is a competing explanation.
hypothesis: An activatable PKM2 pool could restore neural ATP while preserving first recruitment. Lactate alone cannot locate the bottleneck.
experiment: Measure paired glucose-derived PEP and products, absolute ATP recovery and local exposure in null and corrected preparations. Resolve isoform dependence at equal activity.
limits: Conditional ex vivo study. Pediatric evidence comes from PK deficiency. Central exposure, tolerability in WWOX and the useful neural isoform remain uncertain.
